newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - PM WARNS OF INSTABILITY IF EU BID FAILS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - PM WARNS OF INSTABILITY IF EU BID FAILS.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday that the stability of the Baltic region would be threatened if Lithuania was not included in the first round of European Union (EU) enlargement.
Vagnorius said at a news conference that it would be "unjust" to exclude Lithuania from the first wave of EU expansion.
He added that it would pose a danger to the eastern rim of the Baltic Sea.
"Not inviting Lithuania to membership negotiations with other top candiates...would be a dangerous decision which would strongly strike the stability of the Baltic region," he said.
Lithuania and its Baltic neighbours are keen on joing both the EU and NATO as they attempt to shake off the effects of five decades of Soviet hegemony.
Vagnorius defended Lithuania's social and economic record, which he said compared favourably with other EU hopefuls.
"We have lower inflation and unemployment rates and a lower budget deficit than those found in several other candidate countries," he said.
"Our gross domestic product is growing...and we will privatise big state enterprises," he said.
"The government and parliament will focus all of their attention to speeding up the preparations to join the EU," he added.
